outputs.name: transforms
outputs.what: The rotation and translation fields of every ranked prediction row of the arm's docking.out (all fields of the row except the last), in file order.

outputs.name: scores
outputs.what: The score field (the last field) of every ranked prediction row of the arm's docking.out, in file order.

outputs.name: coords
outputs.what: The x, y and z coordinate columns of every ATOM and HETATM record of the arm's assembled models, models taken in rank order.

outputs.name: dockq
outputs.what: The evaluator's DockQ value for each of the arm's assembled models, as one JSON array in rank order, in a file that holds no other number.

metric.name: wall
metric.what: Trusted wall of the invocation: adapter and arm commands, plus the evaluator part.

timing_scope.definition: Trusted wall of each invocation: adapter and arm commands, including reconstruction and assembly, plus evaluator.
timing_scope.unavailable_reason: These additional seed outcomes are not metrics in the supplied s29 comparison view.

evaluator.what: The published DockQ implementation of PINDER (pinder_eval, BiotiteDockQ) at the pinned source, scoring each assembled model of one invocation against the input's native complex with the model's chains R and L mapped to the native's receptor and ligand chains.

spec.private_data: for each input, the native complex named in spec.reference, fetched by fetch_private.sh from its URL and checked against its SHA-256 and byte count. fetch_private.sh is self-contained: it carries each input's reference name, URL, byte count and SHA-256 in its own text and reads no other file under harness/, because only the sealed comparison files and the usual harness scripts are uploaded to the box.
spec.reads: the model_<rank>.pdb files under CMP_ARM_OUT, in rank order; the native complex under CMP_PRIVATE at the name, byte count and SHA-256 given by spec.reference in CMP_INPUT_SPEC
spec.invocation: BiotiteDockQ is constructed with parallel_io=False (models read in the evaluator's own process). evaluate.sh is self-contained: it carries the evaluator's Python program in its own text, writes it at each call to a regular file under CMP_EVAL_OUT, and runs it as the venv interpreter followed by that file's path. It never runs a program read from standard input (PINDER's parallel reader starts its workers with the spawn method, which re-imports the main program from its file) and never runs or reads any other file under harness/, which is not uploaded to the box.
spec.writes: CMP_EVAL_OUT/dockq.json, one JSON array of the DockQ values in rank order and no other number; any per-model detail goes to a separate file under CMP_EVAL_OUT

evaluator.command_reason: The brief prescribes this file-based invocation, not an existing standalone evaluate.sh implementation. BiotiteDockQ must be constructed with parallel_io=False.

scoring_interface.score_output: CMP_EVAL_OUT/dockq.json: one JSON array of DockQ values in rank order, no other number.

budget_policy.reason: No calibrated estimates are supplied and no calibration workload is authorized in intake. Setup, anchors and profile use remaining time before ceiling absent explicit args budgets. No assurance of measured completion time is inferred.

repeatability.seeds_reason: No random seed is specified in the published commands or comparison view.
repeatability.failure_policy: Preserve all invocation files, failures and timeouts; do not rerun outside the pipeline schedule.

contract_limitations: This view has no denser-search arm and excludes the seed apo cases; it cannot answer the seed denser-search recovery question. This is explicitly an s29 fixture recording.
The supplied metric is trusted invocation wall including evaluator. GPU activity, billed allocation cost and complete setup workflow time are not specified as comparison metrics.
No numeric agreement acceptance criterion is supplied; the recording cannot establish tolerance-based scientific agreement from intake alone.
prohibited_intake_actions: No builds, workloads, evaluations, comparative calculations or paid work.
